text:
PagerDuty Bot: PAGER-4321: High GPU queue growth detected for private cluster acme-vpc-1. Severity: P1. Auto-escalating to on-call SRE.
Aisha: I'm oncall, seeing alerts too — queue length jumped from ~120 -> 1900 in 6m.
Aisha: @eng-infra-bot can you post autoscaler status?
eng-infra-bot: autoscaler: scale-loop invoked; desired_nodes=60; current_nodes=12; max_nodes=12; reason=Reached maxNodes limit in cluster-autoscaler config.
Mike: omg max_nodes=12… that explains it. customer workload is bursty - lots of short GPU jobs.
Jordan: Paging customer-success to let customer know potential degradations. @Hana can you DM Acme runbook contact?
Hana: On it, pinged Acme on their support channel and emailed their SRE alias. They confirm they see 500/504s on inference endpoints.
Aisha: Impact summary: Acme production cluster (acme-vpc-1) throttling inference requests -> elevated latency and 5xxs. Backlog currently ~1800 requests waiting. Estimated pending tokens ~3.2M.
Carlos: Root cause candidate: cluster-autoscaler capped by maxNodes=12 + node boot time high (imagepull + init scripts) -> autoscaler can't refill queue. Also found we hit customer cloud quota for instances in their account (VMs per region).
Mike: I can confirm node bootstrap average is ~9-12m based on last 6 instances; combined w/ scale limit that's a death spiral for short bursts.
Aisha: Immediate mitigation options: 1) increase max_nodes for this cluster (requires cust approval/plane change), 2) manually create spare nodes in customer's VPC via support-runbook (if permissions), 3) failover traffic to Redwood Dedicated for urgent requests, 4) prioritize/cancel low-priority jobs in queue. Which do we want to try in parallel?
Jordan: Quick win: drain/cordon low-priority pods and requeue higher-priority ones first. Also request emergency increase of max_nodes to 50 (rollbackable).
Hana: Acme ops replied: they can't raise their quota fast enough in <1h. They asked if we can inject nodes from our Dedicated pool via peered route — security wants a short checklist.
Aisha: Okay, executing three parallel tracks: A) manual prioritization of backlog, B) request emergency policy change to raise max_nodes, C) start Dedicated-fallback plan.
Mike: On A) I'm running a script to identify pods with label "priority=low" and will cordon/evict. Command: 
```
kubectl get pods -n acme-prod -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.metadata.labels.priority}\n'
kubectl -n acme-prod cordon $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=preemptible -o name)
kubectl -n acme-prod evict pod/<low-priority-pod>
```
Mike: Evictions started. Expect gradual backlog drop in ~30-60s per job as scheduler reassigns.
eng-infra-bot: eviction events: 46 pods scheduled for eviction; 22 have completed within 60s; 24 still pending.
Aisha: B) Raising max_nodes — need eng-infra approval. @Carlos can you open change to cluster config? Marking P0.
Carlos: Change request filed: CR-2026-ACME-EMG, requesting max_nodes=50 and temporary auto-scale override window 60m. Applying now through control plane.
eng-infra-bot: control-plane change accepted, new max_nodes=50 pending cluster-autoscaler reconcile.
Mike: C) Dedicated fallback: Jordan, can you spin up an emergency dedicated route for priority inference calls? We'll help route tokens.
Jordan: Starting Dedicated fallback: creating route alias and auth token. ETA ~4m to flip traffic. Note: can only accept up to 400 concurrent GPU streams initially.
Aisha: Monitoring logs: autoscaler loop now sees desired_nodes=46; current_nodes=12 -> scale-up issued. But note: node-provision rate limited by imageregistry (401/429s occasionally).
Mike: I'm seeing imagePullBackOff on new nodes; registry throttling is adding ~90-120s per node. Working with infra provider to ask for push cache.
Hana: Customer reports partial recovery — tail latency improved for some tenants after evictions. But they still see intermittent 5xx when traffic spikes.
Carlos: We have two blockers: (1) customer's VM quota preventing provider-side node creation earlier, (2) node bootstrap delays due to registry throttling + init scripts. Both require longer fixes.
Jordan: Traffic flip to Dedicated fallback complete. Telemetry: 65% of priority inference traffic routed to Dedicated. Error rate for those requests dropped from 18% -> 1.5%. Remaining 35% still hitting private cluster and experiencing 5xx.
Aisha: Customer impact update for Incident War Room: "Acme production inference degraded; majority of critical requests re-routed to Dedicated; non-critical requests experiencing 5xx and delays. Estimated customer-facing SLA impact window: started 2026-03-14T22:05Z, active mitigation until 2026-03-14T22:30Z (ongoing)."
PagerDuty Bot: Incident severity remains P1. Escalation to Eng Lead Nikhil requested.
Mike: Quick mitigation note for runbook: add ability to transparently route a fraction of traffic to Dedicated on per-customer toggle to avoid full cluster dependence.
Hana: Acme asks for post-incident write-up and a timeline. I'll coordinate comms once we stabilize.
Carlos: Longer term next steps (for postmortem): - remove hard max_nodes caps or make them adaptive tied to customer quotas, - reduce node bootstrap time (local registry cache in customer VPC or pre-warmed AMIs), - improve quota/limits check in onboarding, - add predictive scaling for bursty GPU workloads.
Jordan: Handoff: Aisha handing to night oncall Jordan at +00:30Z. Jordan will watch queue until autoscaler finishes and will keep traffic split.
Jordan: I'm taking over. If any new 5xx spikes >5% re-escalate to eng lead Nikhil and open emergency change to cordon remaining low-priority nodes.
Aisha: Thanks team. I'll update incident ticket with actions and attach logs. Leaving channel but reachable via DM. :thumbsup:
Jordan: Confirmed. Monitoring dashboards: queue length down to 420 and trending. Will post another update at +15m or earlier if things regress.
eng-infra-bot: final note: autoscaler reconcile completed; current_nodes=48; new nodes reporting Ready=37, NotReady=11 (imagepull still in progress).
Jordan: Closing initial mitigation phase — continuing observation. Postmortem timeline to follow after incident closure.
PagerDuty Bot: Incident PAGER-4321 remains open.
